recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants exact cross-server text-filter matching semantics rather than documented server-specific behavior, that should be handled as a new terminology issue because it would exceed FHIR-10129's published resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-10129 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification vocab change request asking whether the ValueSet $expand filter definition could be tightened for case sensitivity, punctuation, wildcard handling, starts-with versus contains behavior, and word order. The final decision was to document server-specific behavior through TerminologyCapabilities.expansion.textFilter and add guidance about the kinds of text-filter behavior a terminology server may support.
initial_application: TerminologyCapabilities was added before final publication with an expansion.textFilter element for documenting text-search behavior. The explicit FHIR-10129 application was svn revision 14613, preserved as git commit 4cfb0f493e59259e757035f0908761dfbb470cd2, which added explanatory $expand filter documentation and pointed readers to TerminologyCapabilities.expansion.textFilter. Later source restructuring moved the spreadsheet content into source/valueset/operationdefinition-ValueSet-expand.xml and source/terminologycapabilities/structuredefinition-TerminologyCapabilities.xml while preserving the applied guidance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists both ValueSet and TerminologyCapabilities as active current-build resources. The current $expand filter documentation still delegates matching semantics to the server, points to TerminologyCapabilities.expansion.textFilter, and lists typical matching/search behaviors. TerminologyCapabilities.expansion.textFilter separately asks servers to document case sensitivity, punctuation handling, wildcard support, starts-with versus contains behavior, and word-order handling. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later directly relevant reversal or conflict.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because the authoritative current source already carries the requested clarification at the operation-definition and capability-declaration surfaces.
